strengths: Mathematical fomulation of the proposed method
Details of the proposed deep network based on Encoder-Decoder based on Transformer.
The use of Dual-Aspect Collaborative Attention (DAC-Att)
Comparisons with state of the art (SOA) on MOCOPs.
L2I introduces a new DRL-based approach for MOCOPs.
Unlike the traditional "Learn to Construct" methodology, L2I emphasizes iterative improvements.
The L2I module has demonstrated adaptability as it can be integrated into various MOEA frameworks, such as NSGA-II, MOEA/D, and MOGLS.
This mechanism, applying instance augmentation techniques, improves both the proximity and diversity of the Pareto set.
The L2I methodology outperforms other state-of-the-art techniques on standard MOCOPs, even showing better performance than renowned solutions like the LKH solver for specific problems.
A learning-based improvement method is proposed for solving multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems with deep reinforcement learning.
An ablation study is conducted to study the proposed method and show its effectiveness.
This is the first L2I approach applied to MOCOPs.
A new neural net architecture is introduced, which can accommodate the weight factor used in identifying the Pareto set.
A new RL training method is introduced, leveraging the population pool of the MOEA approach.
A new quality enhancement method suitable for the MOEA approach is presented.
weaknesses: In the result tables, the proposed method is not highlighted
The results in tables 1 & 2 are not discussed on why the proposed approach is better only in the last entries?
Since the paper deals with the combinatorial optimization, decomposition methods are not sufficiently elaborated/reviewed.

The way the proposed weight-related policy network is embedded is not clearly described. A pseudo-code of the complete method for solving one multi-objective combinatorial optimization problem should be provided. Specifically, the interaction between the evolutionary algorithm and the policy network is unclear. It's not evident how the policy network's output influences the selection, crossover, or mutation steps of the evolutionary algorithm. A detailed step-by-step explanation, preferably with pseudo-code, is needed to clarify this integration.

The proposed method contains several hyperparameters, e.g., the number of transformer-style stacked encoders and the number of attention heads. A summary of them needs to be provided. The paper lacks a comprehensive list of all hyperparameters used in the model, including those related to the reinforcement learning component (e.g., learning rate, discount factor, exploration strategy) and the evolutionary algorithm (e.g., population size, crossover and mutation rates). The absence of this information makes it difficult to reproduce the results and assess the method's sensitivity to parameter choices.

How many times does each algorithm run independently in the experiment? The paper should explicitly state the number of independent runs for each algorithm. This is crucial for understanding the statistical significance of the results. Without this information, it's impossible to assess the robustness of the proposed method and the reliability of the comparisons with baseline algorithms.

While the authors have commendably applied the L2I approach to MOCOPs, yielding impressive results, the novelty of the ideas underpinning this work doesn't fully meet the expectations I have for ICRL publications.
The concept of utilizing a trained neural model to bolster the local search component of a genetic algorithm isn't novel.
The presented neural net architecture appears to be a minor variation of an existing one, specifically DACT.
The employment of a shared baseline for REINFORCE isn't groundbreaking, as seen in POMO.
Similarly, quality enhancement via instance augmentation isn't a pioneering approach.
